settings.heading: The long way,
settings.text: Stag and Sole exists because good shoes got expensive for bad reasons. This is how we make them, and why the price is what it is.

settings.heading: A bench in
settings.text: Our workshop has made leather shoes for four decades — first for other people's labels, now for its own. The same family runs the benches. The same hands cut, close, and last every pair. When we say one workshop and no outsourcing, it isn't a slogan; it's the address on the box.

settings.heading: No middlemen
settings.text: A full-grain leather shoe passes through five or six margins before it reaches a shop window. We removed all of them but one — ours. That's the whole trick: the ₹6,000 shoe costs ₹3,499 because nobody else needed paying. Honest pricing, no seasonal markup games.

settings.heading: Built to come
settings.text: Every pair carries a batch stamp traceable to its bench and maker. If a sole wears out, we resole it — twice, on us. Leather that develops a patina instead of cracking, construction that can be opened and repaired, and a workshop that answers for its work. Shoes should come back, not get thrown out.

settings.heading: One workshop.
settings.text: Cutting, skiving, closing, lasting, welting, finishing — forty-two hand steps in one family-run workshop. Slower on purpose, and better for it.

settings.heading: Made to be
settings.text: Everyday shoes on full-grain leather, from our bench to your door.
